newsitem.title: CHINA: Foreign dumping hits Shanghai firms - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Foreign dumping hits Shanghai firms - newspaper.

text.p: Some foreign firms are dumping products in the China market at abnormally low prices and authorities have asked firms hurt by the practice to collect evidence, the Liberation Daily said on Tuesday.
The newspaper said initial investigations indicated foreign dumping was occuring in many different sectors including the chemical industry, metallurgy, pharmaceuticals and construction materials.
"Foreign dumping has caused dozens of Shanghai firms to lose market share with profits falling sharply," the newspaper said. "Some have even been forced to close down."
China last month issued new anti-dumping regulations to protect local companies from unfair competition.

The newspaper said dumping of foreign colour film had forced Shanghai Photo Materials Co to stop production of the film, while Shanghai Sheet Glass Plant has been forced to halt production of centrifugal glass cotton for the same reason.

"Foreign dumping in Shanghai not only involves developed countries but also some developing nations, which try to open the door to China's market by selling products at lower than normal prices," the newspaper said.
"In addition, some foreign firms have used illegal means including smuggling and tax evasion, making the matter even more complicated," it added.
